question.prompt: Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle. Extend side \(\overline{AB}\) beyond \(B\) to a point \(B'\) so that \(BB' = 3 \cdot AB.\) Similarly, extend side \(\overline{BC}\) beyond \(C\) to a point \(C'\) so that \(CC' = 3 \cdot BC,\) and extend side \(\overline{CA}\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(A'\) so that \(AA' = 3 \cdot CA.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle A'B'C'\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.title: Compare areas with shared altitudes
solutions.explanation:
The extensions give bases three times as long as the original sides. Comparing triangles with the same altitude therefore lets us express their areas as multiples of the original area.

Write \([PQR]\) for the area of \(\triangle PQR\), and let \(X=[ABC]\). Connect \(C\) to \(B'\), \(A\) to \(C'\), and \(B\) to \(A'\).

Triangles \(BB'C\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(BB'\) and \(AB\) on the same line and share vertex \(C\), so they have the same altitude. Since \(BB'=3AB\), we get \([BB'C]=3X\). Applying the same comparison around the triangle gives
\[
[BB'C]=[CC'A]=[AA'B]=3X.
\]
Next, triangles \(AA'C'\) and \(ACC'\) share vertex \(C'\), with bases \(AA'\) and \(AC\) on the same line. Since \(AA'=3AC\),
\[
[AA'C']=3[ACC']=3(3X)=9X.
\]
Cycling the vertex labels gives \([CC'B']=9X\) and \([BB'A']=9X\) as well.

To account for the whole outer triangle, its extended side segments separate it into \(ABC\) and the three triangles \(AA'B'\), \(BB'C'\), and \(CC'A'\). Each of these surrounding triangles is split by one of our added segments into a \(3X\) piece and a \(9X\) piece. These pieces have disjoint interiors and fill the outer triangle. Hence
\[
[A'B'C']=X+3(3X+9X)=37X.
\]
The requested ratio is \(\boxed{37:1}\), choice \(\textbf{(E)}\).
